reading_changes: A rating that rests on a premise about the honest operator, such as 'it holds its claim', 'it is always connected' or 'it is always a poster', must check that premise over the whole honest operator's path in section 2, including 'Restarting after a stop (O2)'. A premise that holds only for an operator that never restarts does not support Low.

For a model/deployment disagreement over who may act for a claim, ask whether the honest operator, after a restart on a new identity or connection, is one of the parties that may act in the model. If it is not, the disagreement decides a timeout (A7) and is not harmless.

reading_changes: R12's 'at most linear in ... the bytes it covers' for storing, loading, cloning or syncing a machine refers to the machine (its state, as R12 measures 'from a machine at its starting position'), not to unhashed bytes of the stored directory that a distributor can inflate freely (config.json members, cache capacities); reading it otherwise makes the worst case of loading a fixed machine unbounded and empties 'bounded'.

Section 8's 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator' forbids the possibility: an allocation that scales without bound with unhashed snapshot content violates it even if the prover did not drive a host to an actual crash; do not refute such a finding for 'no crash shown'.

results.severity: Low (best supported); High for hole loads, or Medium for the device load, only if the manual's uarch map is read as exhaustive and as MMIO
results.reason: Manual: uarch "has access to the entire state ... including the main processor and the entire board", and "most of the state is unused and implicitly filled with zeros". Device state is "mapped into the 64-bit physical memory address space" through shadows. Native read_word uses read_memory, which reads unmapped memory as zero. Hole loads are not shown to be R3 traps, and the before-state is unreachable. Decisive fact: whether a normative uarch map excludes holes.

results.severity: Low (preferred) / Medium (if a referee that instantiates by splice or extracts NVRAM results is an in-scope stood-in role)
results.reason: Support library plus demo recipes. prt.lua checks root, address and size itself, so no in-scope component reaches the defect. The stood-in protocol lies outside the model: section 2 says a valid template is "changed only by running it and delivering inputs" (splicing is neither), and A5 allows outputs only via the outputs tree of accepted states. The manual's 'checks M' sentence contradicts its own listing.

frontier_forest refuses heights of 63 and above loudly. The only callers, prt.lua forests, are built by new_geometry, which itself asserts "mcycle_height < 63 and uarch_height < 63". So "A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it" finds none. There is no wrong hash or proof, so no High or Medium case fits.

The manual contradiction is real ("either the current minimum gap or half of it"). I re-simulated consider() for capacities 2 to 32 up to n=200000: the worst gap including the tail stays at or below 2n/capacity, the same bound that the promised spacing allows. The High constant-factor case needs the defect to "multiply the worst-case cost". It does not, so this is "Average-case performance" (out of scope) in the stood-in role. The retention cost itself is R3-VARGROWTH-1.

results.severity: Low (preferred) / Medium (if the manual's 2^24 binds the vg referee)
results.reason: vg.lua is not "The PRT referee model in doc/recipes". Section 5 makes only "The manual's permissionless refereed tournament" normative, so vg is Support. Its player uses the referee's extent, so all parties use 2^16, and A3 ("no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch") holds. No wrong hash results. Decisive fact: whether vg's constants are normative.

Verified: prt.lua calls expand_leaf only from open_bundle, after an opaque get_node_hash or get_siblings. The failure needs a fixed-point base below the expansion height on a node above it. PRT pushes values only at bundle height or above, and finer bases exist only inside bundles. No component reaches it, so "Any other support defect is Low."

reading_changes: When a Support demo stands in for an on-chain verifier of a protocol that the model does not define, first check that the stood-in operation fits the model's protocol. Examples are template instantiation by splicing an NVRAM, result extraction from a halted machine, and the non-PRT verification game with its own constants. Section 2 says a valid template is 'changed only by running it and delivering inputs'. A3 fixes the input path, A5 fixes the output path, and section 5 makes only the PRT model normative. If the stood-in operation falls outside these, no High or Critical rating exists in that role, and the support defect is Low.

Before rating a Support library above Low, check the reachability of each caller in code. Both a guard in the caller (for example the height assert in prt.lua new_geometry) and a call pattern (expand only after an opaque query) can stop every in-scope component from reaching the defect. Under 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it', no reaching component means Low.

Confirmed adjust_starts skips explicit ranges, causing a loud overlap refusal at creation. If 'the manual were right' the machine would be created, but no hash, proof or directory is affected. R4 only requires accepted configs to work, and bad ones to be 'rejected when the machine is created'. The trusted caller can give explicit starts. No listed Medium case fits.

Only the serialization shape differs from the manual. Producers and off-chain verifiers (Support) agree, and the referee uses its own binary encoding. If 'the manual were right', the shape would change but no wrong hash, accepted wrong transition or completeness loss would follow. R13 fixes 'the accesses each logged transition makes, and their order', not the Lua table shape.

Honest-operator component, but the Lua manual says the tail 'supplies the entries of the reverted machine ... when the fixed point is a rejected input'. That describes when it is used and does not make it optional, and cm.h states the precondition. The call fails loudly before any change, and R6 says the operator 'continues from the machine to which the input was delivered', so it can always build the tail. R4 'can always compute the claim' holds.

reading_changes: The application-stall exclusion of section 8 removes only what the application loses. A crash of an operator component (or a support stand-in for one) that a stalled guest triggers is not excluded at step 1 ('The entries about applications exclude what an application loses, never an emulator defect that its guest triggers'). It must be rated at steps 3-4 by asking whether any R4 duty (open disputes, claims, proofs) is still owed.
